text: 4.1.1.2.1 Introduction
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.1 Non-RT RIC architecture related aspects --> 4.1.1.2.1 Introduction
text_preview: 4.1.1.2.1 Introduction

text: In the Decoupled SMO FWID, the standardization of a Service Based Architecture for SMO, as defined in OAD \[i.2\] aims at ensuring the interoperability between components based on the definition of services instead of functions and interfaces. The new approach, however, does neither change the role of the Non-RT RIC nor introduce non-backward compatibility issues over R1 and A1, being the functions defined in the current Non-RT RIC Architecture specification \[i.3\] are one-to-one related to the corresponding services, which can now be referred to a SMOS in OAD \[i.2\].
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.1 Non-RT RIC architecture related aspects --> 4.1.1.2.1 Introduction
text_preview: in the decoupled smo fwid , standardizing service based architecture ( sba ) for smo aims at interoperability based on service definitions instead of functions and interfaces . this approach maintains non - rt ric 's role without introducing backward compatibility issues over r 1 and a 1 , as services are one - to - one related to current non -

text: Both Decoupled SMO Architecture TR \[i.1\] and OAD \[i.2\] state that grouping of SMOS producers in one SMOF is not subject to specification.
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.1 Non-RT RIC architecture related aspects --> 4.1.1.2.1 Introduction
text_preview: Both Decoupled SMO Architecture TR \[i.1\] and OAD \[i.2\] state that grouping of SMOS producers in one SMOF is not subject to specification.

text: Moreover, current Non-RT RIC architecture, shows O1, O2 and Open FH M-Plane interface terminations as distinct functions from the functions providing services to Non-RT RIC. With the introduction Decoupled SMO architecture, as described in OAD \[i.2\] the O1/Open FH M-Plane and O2 interface terminate to RAN NF OAM and NFO/FOCOM SMOS producers, respectively. Hence, Figure 6.1-1 and the definitions of interface terminations should be revised accordingly.
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.1 Non-RT RIC architecture related aspects --> 4.1.1.2.1 Introduction
text_preview: Current Non-RT RIC architecture treats O1, O2, and Open FH M-Plane interface terminations as distinct functions from those providing services to Non-RT RIC. With Decoupled SMO architecture, these interfaces terminate at RAN NF OAM and NFO/FOCOM SMOS producers, respectively.

text:
* Non-RT RIC architecture remains consistent with the overarching Decoupled SMO architecture, improving interoperability and enabling a modular approach to service management.
  * SMOS \(SMO Services\) concept should be integrated into the Non-RT RIC Architecture specification \[i.3\] to ensure it aligns with the Service-Based Architecture \(SBA\) principles of the Decoupled SMO framework.
  * Description of O1/Open FH M-Plane and O2 interfaces and the related services should be adapted to the align with the Decoupled SMO architecture and principles, e.g. by removing the interface termination boxes and refer to the corresponding SMOS producers \(RAN NF OAM and NFO/FOCOM\).
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.1 Non-RT RIC architecture related aspects --> 4.1.1.2.2 Conclusions
text_preview:
The Non-RT RIC architecture aligns with Decoupled SMO, improving interoperability and modular service management.

Integrate SMOS into Non-RT RIC to ensure alignment with SBA principles in Decoupled SMO framework.

Adapt O1/Open FH M-Plane and O2 interfaces to align with Decoupled SMO, removing interface termination boxes.

text: A1 Policy, A1 Enrichment Information and A1-ML Model management \(A1-P, A1-EI, A1-ML\) services are critical for facilitating interaction between the SMO/Non-RT RIC framework and Near-RT RIC through the A1 interface. The management of policies, enrichment information and ML model ensures that near real-time decisions made at the Near-RT RIC are guided or assisted by the management and orchestration services in the SMO/Non-RT RIC.
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.2 A1 related aspects --> 4.1.2.2.1 Introduction
text_preview: A1 Policy, Enrichment Info, and Model Management (A1-P, A1-EI, A1-ML) facilitate interaction between SMO/Non-RT RIC and Near-RT RIC through the A1 interface, ensuring near real-time decisions guided by SMO/Non-RT services.

text: However, there is currently ambiguity about whether producers of these services should be anchored within the Non-RT RIC or be non-anchored \(i.e. flexibly deployable as part of the SMO framework or the NonRT RIC framework\).
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.2 A1 related aspects --> 4.1.2.2.1 Introduction
text_preview: However, there is currently ambiguity about whether producers of these services should be anchored within the Non-RT RIC or be non-anchored \(i.e. flexibly deployable as part of the SMO framework or the NonRT RIC framework\).

text: The introduction of A1 related SMOSs with the exposure of services offered by a function consuming A1 interface services, i.e. A1-P, A1-EI and A1-ML in A1GAP \[i.4\], does not conflict with the A1 interface specifications and with the role of Non-RT RIC, There is however an inconsistency related to the concept of "A1 termination" anchoring, introduced in Non-RT RIC Architecture specification \[i.3\].

text: As for SMOS related to other external SMO interfaces, i.e. O1 and O2, it would be straightforward to assume that the A1 related SMOS producer and the termination of A1 interface are tightly coupled.
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.2 A1 related aspects --> 4.1.2.2.1 Introduction
text_preview: As for SMOS related to other external SMO interfaces, i.e. O1 and O2, it would be straightforward to assume that the A1 related SMOS producer and the termination of A1 interface are tightly coupled.

text: The alternative, i.e. introducing a functional separation between the A1 related SMOS producer and the A1 interface termination, would require the definition of an additional interface or reference point between these to ensure interoperability between the two functions.
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.2 A1 related aspects --> 4.1.2.2.1 Introduction
text_preview: The alternative, i.e. introducing a functional separation between the A1 related SMOS producer and the A1 interface termination, would require the definition of an additional interface or reference point between these to ensure interoperability between the two functions.

text: Before the introduction of SMOS concept, the only consumers of A1 related services were the rApps. With the introduction of other SMOS, e.g. Service Assurance SMOS, also other SMOS producer may consume A1 related services SMOS to e.g. provide policies to Near RT RIC. For this reason, it seems appropriate to expose A1 related services as individual SMOS, as defined in OAD \[i.2\]
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.2 A1 related aspects --> 4.1.2.2.1 Introduction
text_preview: Before SMOS introduction, only rApps consumed A1-related services. With new SMOS like Service Assurance SMOS, other producers can also consume A1 services to provide policies for Near RT RIC. This suggests exposing A1 services as individual SMOS, as defined in OAD [i.2].

text: Following the analysis given above, in order to confirm the assumption that A1 related functions are not anchored to the Non-RT RIC, it is necessary to revise the concept of A1 termination, possibly aligning to other SMO interfaces like O1 and O2, for example avoiding the term "A1 termination function" and use "A1 interface" or "A1 services consumer/producer" instead.
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.2 A1 related aspects --> 4.1.2.2.1 Introduction
text_preview: To confirm the assumption that A1 related functions are not anchored to Non-RT RIC, revise the concept of A1 termination, possibly aligning with O1 and O2 interfaces, e.g., using "A1 interface" or "A1 services consumer/producer".

text: The following paragraphs describe the R1 interface \(Non-RT RIC Architecture specification \[i.3\] clause 6.2\):
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.3 R1 related aspects --> 4.1.3.2.1 R1 Interface
text_preview: The following paragraphs describe the R1 interface \(Non-RT RIC Architecture specification \[i.3\] clause 6.2\):

text: The R1 interface is a service-based interface via which the R1 services can be consumed and produced.
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.3 R1 related aspects --> 4.1.3.2.1 R1 Interface
text_preview: The R1 interface is a service-based interface via which the R1 services can be consumed and produced.

text: The R1 termination enables the R1 Service Producers and R1 Service Consumers to exchange messages via the R1 interface.
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.3 R1 related aspects --> 4.1.3.2.1 R1 Interface
text_preview: The R1 termination enables the R1 Service Producers and R1 Service Consumers to exchange messages via the R1 interface.

text: The R1 termination enables the SMO/Non-RT RIC framework and the rApps to exchange messages via the R1 interface, assuming that the R1 service APIs and the rApps are registered with the R1 service management and exposure functions.
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.3 R1 related aspects --> 4.1.3.2.1 R1 Interface
text_preview: The R1 termination enables the SMO/Non-RT RIC framework and the rApps to exchange messages via the R1 interface, assuming that the R1 service APIs and the rApps are registered with the R1 service management and exposure functions.

text: The R1 interface is clearly identified between SMO/Non-RT RIC Framework and the rApps. This is not changed by the Decoupled SMO Architecture.
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.3 R1 related aspects --> 4.1.3.2.1 R1 Interface
text_preview: The R1 interface is clearly identified between SMO/Non-RT RIC Framework and the rApps. This is not changed by the Decoupled SMO Architecture.

text: 4.1.3.2.2 R1 services
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.3 R1 related aspects --> 4.1.3.2.2 R1 services
text_preview: 4.1.3.2.2 R1 services

text: The following paragraphs describe "R1 services" concepts.
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.3 R1 related aspects --> 4.1.3.2.2 R1 services
text_preview: The following paragraphs describe "R1 services" concepts.

text: From Non-RT RIC Architecture specification \[i.3\] clause 6.2:
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.3 R1 related aspects --> 4.1.3.2.2 R1 services
text_preview: From Non-RT RIC Architecture specification \[i.3\] clause 6.2:

text: The R1 services are a collection of services produced and consumed by logical functions in the SMO/Non-RT RIC framework or by rApps.
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.3 R1 related aspects --> 4.1.3.2.2 R1 services
text_preview: The R1 services are a collection of services produced and consumed by logical functions in the SMO/Non-RT RIC framework or by rApps.

text: The invoker of an R1 service is referred to as R1 Service Consumer and the provider of an R1 service is referred to as R1 Service Producer. R1 Service Consumers can be rApps and/or SMO/Non-RT RIC framework functions. Further, R1 Service Producers can be rApps and/or SMO/Non-RT RIC framework functions.
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.3 R1 related aspects --> 4.1.3.2.2 R1 services
text_preview: The invoker of an R1 service is called a R1 Service Consumer, while the provider is referred to as a R1 Service Producer. Both can be rApps or SMO/Non-RT RIC framework functions.

text: An rApp as well as a SMO/Non-RT RIC framework function can produce zero or more R1 Services, likewise an rApp as well as a SMO/Non-RT RIC framework function can consume zero or more R1 Services.
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.3 R1 related aspects --> 4.1.3.2.2 R1 services
text_preview: An rApp as well as a SMO/Non-RT RIC framework function can produce zero or more R1 Services, likewise an rApp as well as a SMO/Non-RT RIC framework function can consume zero or more R1 Services.

text: From Non-RT RIC Architecture specification \[i.3\] clause 7.1:
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.3 R1 related aspects --> 4.1.3.2.2 R1 services
text_preview: From Non-RT RIC Architecture specification \[i.3\] clause 7.1:

text: The set of R1 services which can be accessed via the R1 interface includes \(but is not limited to\):
trace: 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO --> 4.1.3 R1 related aspects --> 4.1.3.2.2 R1 services
text_preview: The set of R1 services which can be accessed via the R1 interface includes \(but is not limited to\):

text:
* Service management and exposure services, which include service registration and service discovery services, authentication services, authorization services and communication support services. The service management and exposure services support extensibility of the set of R1 services.
  * Data management and exposure services, which deliver data created or collected by Data Producers to Data Consumers according to their needs.
  * A1-related services, which provide access to functionality related to A1.
  * AI/ML workflow services, which provide access to AI and ML workflow.
  * RAN OAM-related services, which provide access to RAN OAM functionality related to the O1 and open fronthaul M-plane interfaces, and to the OAM functionality related to RAN-specific network slicing in the SMO framework.
  * O2-related services, which provide access to functionality related to O2.
  * rApp management services, which provide functionality for managing rApps.
  * TE&IV-related services, which provide access to topology and inventory data.

text: Some of the use cases in UCR \[i.8\] describe the procedures involving SMO components as considering the functional architecture of SMO. text_preview: The following actions are recommended to ensure alignment of WG2 specifications for the introduction of the Decoupled SMO Architecture:

text:
* Introduce SMOS \(SMO Services\) concept into the Non-RT RIC Architecture specification \[i.3\] to ensure it aligns with the Service-Based Architecture \(SBA\) principles of the Decoupled SMO framework and the definition of R1 services.
  * Analyze and align description of O1/Open FH M-Plane and O2 interfaces and the related services in Non-RT RIC Architecture specification \[i.3\] to comply with Decoupled SMO Architectural principles, e.g. by removing the interface termination boxes and refer to the corresponding SMOS producers \(RAN NF OAM and NFO/FOCOM\).
  * Remove the box "A1 termination" from the Non-RT RIC architecture and terminate the A1 interface into the "A1 related functions".
  * Remove the reference to "A1 termination" from clause 8.1 of Non-RT RIC Architecture specification \[i.3\] and replace the remaining two occurrences of "A1 termination" with "A1 interface.
